messages:
Laura Bennett: looping in product on GM targets for Dedicated tiers before we bless pricing bands. we’re seeing a couple assumptions drift (headroom + discounting). can we align today?

Lauren Bishop: yep. thanks @Laura. we’re trying to lock v1 targets for Standard/Plus/Premium for the PRD + enablement. what’s the latest finance view?

Rishi Malhotra: tl;dr we can support tiered commitments, but only if:
1) headroom assumptions are explicit per tier (and enforced), and
2) discount exceptions have a hard gate (deal desk) tied to shape + region.

Laura Bennett: proposing GM targets (blended, incl support allocation + burst reserve):
- Standard: 60% floor
- Plus: 55% floor
- Premium: 50% floor

Laura Bennett: and that’s *after* we allocate burst pool + SRE/CS costs. if we go lower we’re effectively paying for “insurance” without pricing it.

Lauren Bishop: ok. we had earlier draft at 58/52/45 (because premium has HA + warm pool). what’s driving the tighter targets now?

Rishi Malhotra: two things changed since the workshop:
- GPU COGS for H100 in us-east + eu-central is higher than the sheet assumed (and lead times mean we’ll carry more idle capacity)
- burst behavior is trending higher in early Dedicated accounts (we’re reserving more “shadow” capacity than we priced)

Lauren Bishop: got it. can we talk headroom since that’s the biggest lever? we need premium to be meaningfully safer.

Vanessa Ortiz: (fleet) sharing the current headroom model we’ve been using for planning:
- Standard: 20–25% headroom (can overbook modestly with admission control)
- Plus: 30–35% headroom (limited overbook)
- Premium: 45–55% headroom (no overbook; plus N+1 spare per pool in a couple regions)

Vanessa Ortiz: if premium is truly “throughput floor holds even during local failures”, we’re basically committing to spare nodes + faster replacements.

Laura Bennett: +1. finance is fine funding that, but it needs to show up in price and/or GM target can’t drop below ~50% or we’ll miss overall dedicated margin plan.

Lauren Bishop: ok. one nuance: premium language we’re drafting is “stronger failover posture” not “always survive node loss”. we were planning to avoid hard HA promises in v1.

Irene Choi: from infra side, we can do:
- premium: warm pool + faster failover to same region pool (if capacity)
- cross-region failover only “best effort” unless we reserve it (expensive)

Irene Choi: so if product commits to no cross-region guarantee, premium headroom might be closer to 40–45% vs 55%.

Rishi Malhotra: that helps. finance’s biggest concern is premium quietly becoming “we reserve double capacity everywhere”. we need contract language to cap the promise.

Lauren Bishop: makes sense. I’ll adjust premium entitlement language to be explicit: no cross-region guaranteed throughput floor unless add-on.

Laura Bennett: great. then we can align headroom assumptions as:
Standard: 25%
Plus: 35%
Premium: 45% (assuming no cross-region guarantee)

Laura Bennett: can we also agree on utilization targets (steady-state) for the model? we’re using:
- Standard: 70% target utilization
- Plus: 65%
- Premium: 55%

Lauren Bishop: yes, those seem consistent with tier differentiation.

Lauren Bishop: question on discounts: sales is going to ask for flexibility for multi-year commits + logo deals. what’s acceptable without deal desk?

Isabelle Laurent: (sales ops) jumping in — AEs asked for a simple rubric. can finance propose “self-serve” discount bands and then explicit triggers?

Laura Bennett: yes. suggested guardrails (off list):
- Standard: up to 10% w/ manager approval
- Plus: up to 8%
- Premium: up to 5%

Laura Bennett: deal desk required if any of:
- discount > band above
- requesting non-standard headroom (e.g., “premium in us-east on H100 with dedicated spare nodes”)
- region w constrained supply (eu-central H100, ap-south anything)
- asking for burst included above standard policy

Rishi Malhotra: also deal desk if the request implies GM < target OR if they want to lock in pricing for a new shape we haven’t benchmarked.

Lauren Bishop: ok. we should translate that into “what sales can say” language. AEs hate “GM model says no.”

Isabelle Laurent: +1. we can phrase triggers as “non-standard terms” + “supply constrained regions” rather than margin.

Laura Bennett: totally. internally we’ll evaluate vs GM targets; externally it’s “requires review due to capacity constraints and support commitments”.

Lauren Bishop: re: discounting for multi-year— can we do more if it’s a 24–36mo commit?

Rishi Malhotra: we can, but it should be structured as:
- higher commit gets lower effective price *only if* utilization assumption improves (e.g., 36mo gives us planning certainty)
- otherwise you’re just giving away margin.

Laura Bennett: propose rule of thumb:
- additional 2–3% discount allowed for 36mo terms (still subject to GM floor)
- any “logo exception” beyond that needs CFO sign-off (or VP Finance delegate)

Lauren Bishop: ok. can you sanity check the tier price bands if we adopt 60/55/50 GM targets? I don’t want to rework packaging twice.

Laura Bennett: yes, but with one condition: premium must not include “free cross-region failover”. if that stays out, we can price premium to maintain 50% with 45% headroom.

Irene Choi: infra note: if sales tries to sell premium in eu-central on H100 *this quarter*, lead time risk is real. we should make sure deal desk trigger calls that out.

Isabelle Laurent: capturing: “eu-central H100 premium = mandatory deal desk due to supply/lead time.”

Lauren Bishop: sounds good. action items:
1) @Lauren to update premium entitlement language (no cross-region guarantee in v1; define failover posture)
2) @Laura/@Rishi to share GM targets + discount guardrails in a blurb we can paste into pricing doc + enablement
3) @Vanessa/@Irene to confirm headroom defaults (25/35/45) are supportable w planned routing/admission control

Laura Bennett: works. I’ll send a short write-up + we’ll align with Legal on “discount exceptions” being consistent w order form language.

Rishi Malhotra: also flagging: if we see burst > X% of committed in early cohorts, we may need to revisit plus/premium list. not a blocker but we should monitor.

Lauren Bishop: agree. we’re adding burst metering + dashboard in the rollout plan. will share once observability has a draft.

Laura Bennett: :thumbsup: thanks all. please keep finance in the loop before promising “special pricing” on premium shapes.

Isabelle Laurent: noted. I’ll update the deal desk checklist + AE cheat sheet to match these bands.

Vanessa Ortiz: :eyes: I’ll confirm the headroom numbers with Jamal and post back if anything looks off for 2026H1 forecast.

Lauren Bishop: thx. closing loop once I’ve pushed the updated language.
